Aave, Ethena and Hyperliquid Founders on Their Biggest Competitors (Archive Video)

At a TOKEN2049 Singapore roundtable on October 14, 2025, Aave founder Stani Kulechov @StaniKulechov  , Ethena founder Guy Young @gdog97_ , and Hyperliquid co-founder Jeff Yan @chameleon_jeff   were asked who they saw as their biggest competitors. Their answers were "the banks," "Circle," and "nobody," respectively.

Coinbase, Which Holds About 5% of Existing BTC in Custody, Outlines Bitcoin Post-Quantum Security Recommendations

Coinbase, which holds approximately 5% of all existing BTC in custody, outlined technical considerations for Bitcoin’s transition to post-quantum security. The company warned that the migration could take years and urged early preparations. Coinbase suggested exploring flexible output designs such as BIP-360 (P2MR) and P2TRv2, alongside a phased transition supporting both classical and post-quantum signature mechanisms. It also emphasized that questions surrounding dormant funds, lost private keys, and wallets that fail to migrate should be addressed separately to avoid delaying broader post-quantum security upgrades.

Solana’s Alpenglow Upgrade Scheduled for October 21, Targets Finality Cut from 12.8 Seconds to 150ms

Solana core developer Anza announced that the Alpenglow consensus upgrade is scheduled to go live on Solana mainnet-beta on October 21 at approximately 14:50 UTC. The upgrade will replace the existing TowerBFT consensus mechanism with Votor, aiming to reduce transaction finality from approximately 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds. Under the new mechanism, validators will exchange votes directly instead of submitting them as onchain transactions, potentially causing a significant decline in reported transaction totals that include validator votes. Alpenglow was previously activated on testnet on September 24 and devnet on September 25.

Sui Devnet Adds Post-Quantum Signature Support, Targets Mainnet Rollout in Q1 2027

Mysten Labs co-founder and chief cryptographer Kostas Chalkias announced that Sui Devnet has successfully processed its first native quantum-safe transaction, sharing the on-chain transaction record. Sui's core developer Mysten Labs has introduced ML-DSA-65 post-quantum signature support in Devnet release v1.82.0, allowing signed transactions to be submitted through the ExecuteTransaction API and verified through the VerifySignature API.

ML-DSA-65 is also supported in multisignature transactions, with additional integration into GraphQL and the Rust SDK. According to Sui's previously announced roadmap, native ML-DSA-65 accounts are expected to reach Testnet by the end of 2026, with native account authentication on Mainnet targeted for Q1 2027, subject to security audits and testing results.

Wintermute: Crypto Is Losing Its Flow Support as ETF Outflows Mount

Wintermute said crypto is losing support from capital flows, while equities remain backed by earnings expectations. Last week, BTC fell 3.2% and ETH dropped 7.0%, with U.S. spot BTC and ETH ETFs recording $679M and $542M in net outflows, respectively. BTC ETF outflows were the largest weekly total since late June.

Wintermute said a sustained recovery requires long-term Treasury yields to stabilize and spot ETF flows to turn positive. Until then, BTC remains vulnerable to volatility and downside risks, while low-quality altcoin rallies should be approached cautiously. The firm remains constructive long term but would turn more cautious if the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield exceeds 5.64% or BTC repeatedly fails to break above $82,500.
